question.prompt: A right rectangular prism whose surface area and volume are numerically equal has edge lengths \(\log_2 x,\) \(\log_3 x,\) and \(\log_4 x.\) What is \(x?\)

solutions.title: Use reciprocal logarithms
solutions.explanation:
Dividing surface area by volume turns products of edge lengths into reciprocals, which combine neatly using logarithms.

Let
\[
a=\log_2x,\qquad b=\log_3x,\qquad c=\log_4x.
\]
All three edge lengths are positive, so \(x>1\). The surface area and volume are \(2(ab+bc+ca)\) and \(abc\), respectively. Their equality gives
\[
2(ab+bc+ca)=abc.
\]
Since \(abc>0\), we may divide by it to obtain
\[
2\left(\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c\right)=1.
\]
The change-of-base formula gives \(1/\log_bx=\log_xb\). Consequently,
\[
\log_x2+\log_x3+\log_x4=\frac12.
\]
Logarithms with the same base add by multiplying their arguments, so
\[
\log_x24=\frac12.
\]
By the definition of a logarithm, this means \(x^{1/2}=24\). Hence
\[
x=24^2=\boxed{576},
\]
which is choice E.

solutions.title: Express all edges in one base
solutions.explanation:
Changing every logarithm to base \(2\) expresses all three edges as fixed multiples of one unknown length.

Set \(t=\log_2x\) and \(r=\log_23\). Positive edge lengths imply \(x>1\), so \(t>0\); also \(r>0\). By change of base, the three edges are
\[
t,\qquad \frac{t}{r},\qquad \frac{t}{2}.
\]
The surface area is therefore
\[
2\left(\frac{t^2}{r}+\frac{t^2}{2r}+\frac{t^2}{2}\right)
=t^2\left(1+\frac3r\right),
\]
and the volume is
\[
\frac{t^3}{2r}.
\]
Equating them and multiplying by \(2r/t^2\), which is defined because \(t>0\), gives
\[
2r+6=t.
\]
Returning to logarithms,
\[
\log_2x=6+2\log_23
=\log_2(2^6)+\log_2(3^2)
=\log_2(64\cdot9).
\]
Thus
\[
x=64\cdot9=\boxed{576},
\]
which is choice E.
